title: Artifact Restoration Lab
description: The user operates a futuristic restoration lab where a DamagedHelmet sits on a pedestal under an IridescenceLamp. By manipulating the lamp's position, intensity, color temperature, and beam angle, the user must illuminate specific damaged regions of the helmet, then apply repair pulses to restore them. A diagnostic HUD tracks restoration progress across multiple damage zones.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive artifact restoration lab. Load DamagedHelmet.glb centered on a circular metallic pedestal at origin and IridescenceLamp.glb positioned above-right at (2, 3, 1). Use GLTFLoader from three/addons. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2, 5) looking at the helmet with OrbitControls for viewing. Add ambient light at intensity 0.15 and a SpotLight parented to the lamp model acting as its functional beam. Create an HTML overlay HUD panel showing: lamp X/Y/Z position sliders (range -4 to 4), intensity slider (0 to 5), color temperature slider (2700K to 8500K mapped to warm-orange through cool-blue), beam angle slider (10 to 80 degrees), and a Repair Pulse button. Define 6 damage zones as invisible sphere regions on the helmet surface at predefined local coordinates. Each zone has a name label and requires specific illumination conditions: the SpotLight must point within 15 degrees of the zone center AND intensity must exceed 2.0 AND beam angle must be narrow enough (under 40 degrees) to be considered targeted. When a zone is properly targeted, highlight it with a green wireframe sphere and enable the Repair Pulse button. Clicking Repair Pulse triggers a 1-second animation where a glowing expanding ring emanates from the lamp toward the zone, the zone sphere flashes white, then marks as restored in the HUD with a checkmark. The HUD displays a progress bar showing zones restored out of 6. Track that the user must: position the lamp to target zone 1, fire repair pulse, reposition for zone 2, adjust intensity above threshold, fire pulse, adjust beam angle for zone 3, fire pulse, change color temperature for zone 4 targeting, fire pulse, combine multiple parameter changes for zones 5 and 6 with pulses. After all 6 zones are restored, display a completion banner reading Restoration Complete with a golden particle burst effect around the helmet. Use a dark environment with subtle grid floor. Ensure the lamp model visually rotates to track its SpotLight direction.
